competitors.title: Portkey AI Gateway Documentation
key_points: Open-source AI gateway with universal API for 100+ models via REST and SDKs
Conditional routing based on metadata, request parameters, and URL pathname with $eq/$ne/$in/$regex/$gt/$lt operators
Load balancing with weighted distribution, sticky sessions (Redis-backed), and cross-provider routing
Fallback chains with multi-tier fallback, status-code-specific triggers, and automatic retry strategies
Circuit breaker with per-strategy protection and failure handling
Simple cache (exact match) and semantic cache (cosine similarity, default 0.95 threshold) for 20x faster responses
Configs as JSON objects that define routing rules, attachable via SDK or x-portkey-config header
Self-hostable via npx @portkey-ai/gateway with Docker and Helm chart support
MCP Gateway for agent tool connectivity, Agent Gateway for agent governance

competitors.title: LiteLLM Router Documentation
key_points: Open-source unified interface for 100+ LLMs using OpenAI-compatible format
Router with multiple routing strategies: weighted pick (default), rate-limit aware, latency-based, least-busy, lowest-cost
Load balancing across multiple deployments (Azure/OpenAI/bedrock) with RPM/TPM-aware shuffling
Automatic fallbacks, cooldowns, timeouts, and retries (fixed + exponential backoff) across deployments
Redis-based cooldown tracking and usage management for production scale
Self-hosted Proxy Server with virtual keys, cost tracking, admin UI, and guardrails
Agent & MCP Gateway: unified gateway for LLMs, agents (A2A), and MCP tools from one endpoint
Enterprise features: SSO/SAML, audit logs, budget limits, rate limits per key/team/user

competitors.title: Beyond the Hype: The Enterprise AI Blueprint — Why Your AI Gateway is Non-Negotiable
key_points: Five critical gateway functions: orchestration, observability, governance, model management, integration
Intelligent model routing: queries auto-directed to most appropriate model based on language, domain, and complexity
50-70% reduction in individual R&D costs through strategic ecosystem partnerships
Two-year roadmap: Year 1 establish foundational capabilities, Year 2 optimize proprietary models
Enterprise AI trilemma: generic models lack domain expertise, custom models prohibitively expensive, fine-tuning more complex than advertised
Gateway as essential infrastructure preventing fragmentation across multi-model deployments

competitors.title: Portkey Conditional Routing Documentation
key_points: Route requests to different provider targets based on custom conditions: user plan, model parameter, geographic region, temperature threshold
Conditions evaluate metadata (custom key-value pairs), request parameters (model, temperature, max_tokens), and URL pathname
Supported operators: $eq, $ne, $in, $nin, $regex, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte
Logical operators: $and (all conditions must be true), $or (at least one must be true), mixed nesting supported
All routing happens on the gateway at edge, very fast
Configs are composable: conditional routing can be combined with fallbacks and load balancing

competitors.title: Portkey Load Balancing Documentation
key_points: Distribute traffic across multiple LLMs for high availability and optimal performance
Four load balancing patterns: between providers, multiple API keys, cost optimization, gradual migration
Weight normalization: weights sum to 100% automatically (e.g., 5/3/1 becomes 55%/33%/11%)
Sticky load balancing: consistent routing by user_id or session_id with configurable TTL (default 3600s)
Composable with conditional routing and fallbacks as nested strategies

competitors.title: Portkey Cache Documentation
key_points: Simple cache: exact match on full request body including messages, model, temperature, max_tokens
Semantic cache: cosine similarity matching for semantically similar requests (default threshold 0.95)
Cache serves requests up to 20x faster than uncached LLM calls
Semantic cache ignores system prompt changes, requires at least one user message
Self-hosted semantic cache requires embedding provider + vector database (Milvus or Pinecone)
Cache TTL configurable per config, force-refresh via x-portkey-cache-force-refresh header

angles: The 85/10/5 model routing rule: matching task complexity to model tier (cheap for 85% of queries, mid-tier for 10%, frontier for 5%) achieves ~92% savings vs all-frontier approach
Three-layer caching stack: exact-match cache for repeated identical prompts, semantic cache for paraphrased queries, prompt caching for system prompt reuse — compounds savings across all query types
Conditional routing as the control plane: route by user plan (free vs paid), geographic region (EU data residency), model parameter (fastest vs smartest), or environment (testing vs production)
Circuit breaker patterns for production resilience: per-strategy protection prevents cascading failures when a provider degrades, with automatic recovery and fallback chains

Load balancing strategies: between providers for high availability, across multiple API keys to avoid rate limits, cost optimization by sending most traffic to cheaper models, gradual migration for canary testing new models
The hidden cost of not routing: 40-60% of token budgets are pure waste when every query hits the most expensive model — routing is the single highest-leverage cost optimization
Gateway vs SDK routing: architectural tradeoffs between centralized gateway control (Portkey, LiteLLM Proxy) and client-side SDK routing (LiteLLM Router) — latency overhead vs governance granularity
Sticky sessions for agentic workloads: maintaining conversation context across multi-turn agent interactions by consistently routing the same user/session to the same model deployment
